agent_messages.text: I’ll read the pinned goal, design, audits, and latest evidence, then choose a research step and checkpoint the results. The active filesystem policy denies `.scratch`, so I’ll use a new directory under `research/` for temporary work and record that limitation.

The latest completed run proves support and endpoint formulas, but leaves the residual inequalities open. It also found two useful limits: some enlarged palindromic words fail log-concavity, and individual terms of the positive recurrence can have negative mixed gaps. I’ll test whether grouping the recurrence terms gives a viable invariant for actual source words.

Reconciliation passed: the latest run’s 97 artifacts and the interrupted worker’s 1,355 surviving artifacts match their recorded hashes. I have not replayed any prior action. The new probe is checking grouped updates on source-word prefixes; it will show whether grouping removes the mixed-term obstruction.

The prefix probe found a stronger obstruction: on a prefix of the actual source word for \(2/23\), an auxiliary \(F\)-row contains \([2,5,13]\), so \(5^2<2\cdot13\). Thus an induction requiring both states to be log-concave at every prefix cannot work. This does not refute the source polynomial’s inequality. I’ll formalize that obstruction and check the rescaling back to raw coefficients at high indices.

A second exact probe found a raw diagonal failure in a prefix of the \(11/13\) source word: \([10,14,20]\), with \(14^2<10\cdot20\). That prefix has letter counts \(7/9\), but it is not the \(7/9\) source word; the actual \(7/9\) coefficients there are \([4,12,20]\) and satisfy the inequality. This rules out extending the target to all source prefixes, even with polygon guards retained.

The new Lean modules compile. They prove the raw-prefix failure and its exclusion from the source-word family, an unbounded family of auxiliary \(F\)-prefix failures, and the exact raw/residual rescaling identity for every word beginning with A. The identity preserves the high-index factor in the correct direction; it gives no backward cancellation of log-concavity. I’m checking the source adapters and theorem closures next.

The source adapters compile, including the checked distinction between the failing prefix and the actual \(7/9\) polynomial. The axiom audit initially rejected its receipt because the inherited parser did not recognize Lean’s “does not depend on any axioms” output. I corrected this run’s parser and reran validation. The mathematical proofs did not change for that fix.

Validation passed for all seven new modules and all 40 theorem closures. The raw-prefix scan was also rerun with zero centers included: 11,447,217 comparisons found the same 257 diagonal failures, all on prefixes rather than completed source words. The pinned root remains unresolved. I’m recording the final evidence and revised agenda.
